teaching_note: FININT analysis separates transaction observations, entity-resolution hypotheses and claims about purpose or legality. A payment, a network edge and a beneficial-owner conclusion require different evidence; access to a public registry does not authorize unrestricted aggregation or prove the registry is complete or current. The two inherited encyclopedia links share a source family and are not two independent authorities for a financial or legal conclusion.
title: FININT Foundations: Collection, Analysis, Reporting

raw: 17.2 Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs) and Financial Intelligence Units[^79]
teaching_note: A suspicious-activity report records a reporting suspicion, not a conviction or proof that the named party committed an offence; reporting institutions and FIUs have distinct submission and analytic roles. Reporting triggers, confidentiality, eligible recipients and FIU powers depend on jurisdiction, institution type and the dated rule; the inherited encyclopedia summary cannot establish a current threshold. In a fictional applicability card, an archive extract dated 2024 covers entity class C, while a supplied later body notice dated 2026 expressly exempts C: a missing C filing cannot be treated as noncompliance under the obsolete card. This demonstrates checking effective dates, exceptions and operative body text rather than relying on stale metadata, not a claim about any real jurisdiction's exemptions. Work only with fictional abstracts; do not obtain, disclose or file real reports.
title: Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs) and Financial Intelligence Units

teaching_note: A typology describes a possible pattern, not terrorist purpose, a prohibited recipient or criminal conduct; subscriptions and donations can explain repeated small payments. In a fictional packet, three 20-unit transfers on consecutive dates have no list match, while invoice I1 explains two as scheduled instalments and the third lacks context. The result is 'two transfers explained by supplied invoices; third unresolved', not 'clean because no hit' or 'terrorist financing because repeated'; currency, time and counterparty context are still required. A list non-match cannot bypass transaction-context review, and a red flag cannot establish guilt. No interdiction, live monitoring or operational response follows from the classroom disposition.
title: Terrorist Financing: Identification, Typologies, Interdiction

raw: 17.4 The SWIFT System and Intelligence Collection[^79]
teaching_note: SWIFT is a financial messaging system; a message about an instructed payment is not by itself proof of settlement, beneficiary control or unlawful purpose. Distinguish instruction, message transmission, account posting and final settlement in supplied fictional records. The general FININT reference is not a technical SWIFT specification or collection authority, so current message-field semantics and access powers remain unknown without appropriate dated extracts.
title: The SWIFT System and Intelligence Collection

raw: 17.5 Cryptocurrency as Covert Finance: Monero, Mixers, Bridges
teaching_note: A cryptocurrency address is not a verified person, and an address cluster is a model-dependent linkage rather than beneficial-owner proof. A bridge transfers representations across systems, while privacy mechanisms can limit observable linkage; use of either does not establish the covert or criminal purpose implied by the raw inherited heading. The FATF 2021 guidance supplies dated virtual-asset and VASP risk-governance context [@ageint315], not protocol-specific tracing or ownership proof; its official page excludes later revisions, including the 2025 changes to Recommendation 1. Specific protocol capabilities and present legal status remain unverified here. This course excludes live wallet lookup, tracing real people and evasion instructions.
title: Cryptocurrency Records: Privacy, Transfers and Inference Limits

raw: 17.6 Economic Warfare and FININT as a Strategic Tool[^81]

Even a conceptual workflow must keep entity matching, list/programme applicability, transaction context and ownership uncertainty as separate checks; a no-hit result cannot automatically clear the other questions.
title: Economic Warfare and FININT as a Strategic Tool

raw: 17.7 Money Laundering Detection: Data Mining and Matching Techniques[^80]
teaching_note: In a completed synthetic packet, E1 ('Orion Parts', jurisdiction J, ID 11) and E2 ('ORION PARTS', jurisdiction K, ID 22) share a normalized name and address, list L1 names J/11, and transaction T supplies only the name: normalization produces two candidates, not one resolved counterparty, since a shared office address also need not imply control. The result for T is 'name match; list applicability and ownership unknown', with no guilt or blocking conclusion. Fictional classroom extracts dated 2026-01-01 use a same-ID ownership flag of at least 50% in J and at least 25% in K; for a separate E1-only record stating one relevant owner's 40%, J's stated flag is not triggered, K's rule cannot be substituted across jurisdictions, and missing other ownership interests prevents a clearance conclusion. E2 is the negative control against name/address-only joining; changing E1's supplied share to 60% changes J's classroom flag only, while removing ID/jurisdiction stops classification instead of prompting a live lookup. All entities, percentages and rules are invented teaching inputs, not real legal thresholds, and neither a flag nor its absence proves beneficial ownership, sanctions status or money laundering.
title: Money Laundering Detection: Data Mining and Matching Techniques

raw: 17.8 FININT Supporting National Security: Pillars and Methods[^82]
teaching_note: An institutional account can propose that coordination improves resilience without measuring that causal effect or supplying legal authority for data sharing. Distinguish a paper's conceptual framework, documented information flow and independently evaluated outcome; a broad national-security rationale does not remove privacy or due-process limits. This inherited paper is not a substitute for dated legislation, a sanctions determination or an empirical accuracy study, so those claims remain outside its established support.
title: FININT Supporting National Security: Pillars and Methods
